blog_summary: Adrian Colyer reviews Howard's PhD thesis on distributed consensus, which revises and generalizes the classic Paxos algorithm. The thesis weakens quorum intersection requirements, allowing more flexible phase interactions and value selection rules. Key insights include relaxing the need for all quorums to intersect, enabling phase-two bypass optimizations, and introducing epoch-specific quorums. The work also explores flexible epoch allocation strategies and combinations of mechanisms to optimize performance and availability trade-offs. Colyer highlights the thesis's contribution to expanding the Paxos family of algorithms, offering finer-grained trade-offs and broader progress conditions, with practical implications for distributed systems.
